verdict.reasoning: Patient says the room is spinning and it has been present continuously for about two hours: “Started probably about two hours ago maybe… Yeah it's, it's there, the whole time… So it's there now for the past two hours you'd say, yeah? – Yep.”
Onset occurred while making breakfast with fuzziness, dizziness, and shakiness: “I was just actually making my husband some breakfast… I just suddenly felt very fuzzy and dizzy, um, and a bit shaky.”
Unsteady gait described: “I can't, I can't walk properly. Uh, well I can walk properly but not straight… I don't feel like I'm stable. My, the room is spinning.”

Ear buzzing without pain, discharge, or hearing loss: “my ears are buzzing a bit”… “Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge, anything like that? – No, nothing.” and “do you have any problems hearing…? – No… It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears, but otherwise I can hear everything.” Laterality (bilateral) is not specified but ear buzzing is plausibly both ears; no contradiction.
Nausea without vomiting: “Have you been physically sick? – No, but now I'm feeling very sick. – Nausea, OK.”

No recent viral illness, cough, or cold; temperature uncertain but no fever reported: “Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past…? – No. – No cold, cough, nothing. – No, I've been pretty healthy…” and “Do you have a temperature at all? – I don't think so.”

Similar brief episode a month ago lasting 5–10 minutes: “I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago… it settled quite quickly.” and “how long did that episode last for? – Probably only about five, ten minutes.”

No limb weakness or focal neurological features: “My, my legs and arms and everything are working fine… So there's no weakness of your arms and legs. OK. – No.” No other focal neurological deficits are mentioned.
Premature ovarian failure is stated: “I've had premature ovarian failure…”
Use of HRT is stated: “I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT.”
No allergies: “OK, do you have any allergies at all? – No.”

Summary matches: acute vertigo with tinnitus (buzzing), about 2 hours, no focal deficits, and similar episode 1 month ago: supported by earlier quotes on room spinning for 2 hours, “my ears are buzzing,” “no weakness of your arms and legs,” and prior 5–10 minute episode a month ago.
Working diagnosis is labyrinthitis: “the most common… diagnosis… is something called labyrinthitis. Yeah?”

Nausea is linked to vertigo symptoms: patient ties feeling very sick to dizziness (“I'm feeling very sick. It's probably because i'm feeling dizzy”), and doctor frames treatment as for vertigo; nausea is secondary to vertigo by direct patient statement.
Premature ovarian failure treated with HRT: “I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT.”

Vestibular suppressant (unnamed) prescribed 1 tablet TID for 10 days to Lloyds Pharmacy: “we'll start you on certain medications… So i'll, i'll send the a prescription… looks like it's the Lloyd pharmacy… It's called , yeah? It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about ten days worth.”

Plan for in-person review including ears, BP, and gait/neuro: “I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears… while you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how your walking and everything is.” Gait assessment implies basic neuro assessment.

Safety net to attend A&E if limb weakness, sudden headache, or violent vomiting: “if you double up any weakness of your legs or arms or, or, you know, a sudden headache… or you start being violently sick with it, then… you would need to take your to A and E.”
Medication with or without food: “can you take, do you need to take those tablets with food? Or can you just take them any time? – It doesn't really matter, you can take it…”

Patient to call support to book appointment and follow-up after in-person assessment: “while you're with the doctors…” and “Just make sure you call support to book that appointment, OK?” plus earlier plan “In the interim, obviously in the next few days, you'll get to see one of my doctors and we'll have to just take it from there.”
